Article Title: Quote of the Day by Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor who inspired Gladiator: "You have power over your mind, not outside events..."
Article Text:
Image: Getty Images

Quote of the Day by Marcus Aurelius: "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength."

Who was Marcus Aurelius?

The Stoic philosophy behind the quote



Why the quote remains relevant today



Lessons readers can apply in daily life

A timeless reminder from ancient Rome

Many people recognise Marcus Aurelius as the wise Roman emperor whose fictionalised character inspired Ridley Scott's Gladiator. Yet long before Hollywood brought ancient Rome to the big screen, Marcus Aurelius had earned a place in history as one of the greatest Stoic philosophers and one of Rome's most respected rulers. His private writings, later compiled as Meditations, continue to inspire millions around the world with their timeless reflections on resilience, discipline and inner peace. Among his most enduring observations is: "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength." Although written nearly 2,000 years ago, the quote remains remarkably relevant in a world shaped by uncertainty, social media pressures and constant change.At its heart, Marcus Aurelius' quote is a reminder that while people cannot control everything that happens around them, they can control how they respond. Life is full of unexpected challenges, from personal disappointments and workplace stress to global events beyond anyone's influence. According to Stoic philosophy, peace comes not from trying to change external circumstances but from mastering one's own thoughts and reactions.The second part of the quote, "Realise this, and you will find strength," explains where genuine resilience comes from. Strength is not measured by physical power or status but by emotional stability and the ability to remain calm when circumstances become difficult.Marcus Aurelius ruled the Roman Empire from AD 161 until his death in AD 180. He is remembered as the last of Rome's "Five Good Emperors" and led the empire during a period marked by wars, political challenges and outbreaks of disease. Despite carrying enormous responsibilities, he found time to write personal reflections that would later become Meditations, one of history's most influential philosophical works.Unlike books written for publication, Meditations was intended as a private journal. Marcus Aurelius used it to remind himself how to live with integrity, patience and humility. The honesty of these writings has allowed readers across centuries to relate to his struggles and wisdom.Although Gladiator introduced Marcus Aurelius to modern audiences, the film took considerable creative liberties. In reality, he was not murdered by his son Commodus, as portrayed in the movie. Historians believe he died of illness while leading military campaigns near the empire's northern frontier.Marcus Aurelius belonged to the Stoic school of philosophy, which taught that happiness depends more on character than on external success. Stoicism encourages individuals to focus only on what lies within their control while accepting everything else with courage and wisdom.This philosophy divides life into two categories. The first includes things people can influence, such as their decisions, attitudes, values and actions. The second includes everything beyond their control, including other people's behaviour, the weather, economic conditions and unexpected setbacks.Marcus Aurelius believed much of human suffering comes from confusing these two categories. People often exhaust themselves trying to control circumstances they cannot change instead of improving the one thing they truly possess: their own mind.Modern life presents countless situations that reinforce Marcus Aurelius' advice. People worry about social media opinions, office politics, financial uncertainty or events unfolding across the world. While these concerns are understandable, obsessing over them rarely changes the outcome.The quote encourages a healthier approach. Rather than allowing outside events to dictate emotions, individuals can choose patience, rational thinking and self-control. This mindset often leads to better decision-making because reactions are guided by reason instead of fear or anger.Psychologists also recognise that focusing on controllable actions helps reduce stress and anxiety. Although Marcus Aurelius lived nearly two millennia before modern psychology emerged, his observations closely resemble concepts used today in cognitive behavioural therapy, which teaches people to challenge unhelpful thoughts and focus on constructive responses.Marcus Aurelius' wisdom is practical rather than abstract. The quote can be applied in everyday situations.When criticism arises, people cannot always control what others say, but they can choose whether to let those words define them. When plans fail, they cannot rewrite the past, but they can decide how to move forward. During periods of uncertainty, they cannot predict every outcome, but they can prepare thoughtfully and respond calmly.This perspective does not encourage ignoring problems or avoiding responsibility. Instead, it reminds people to invest their energy where it can make a meaningful difference. By concentrating on personal growth, discipline and thoughtful action, individuals often become more resilient and effective.Nearly 2,000 years after Marcus Aurelius wrote Meditations, his reflections continue to influence readers ranging from business leaders and athletes to military officers and students. His ideas have survived because they address universal human experiences that remain unchanged despite technological and social progress.The quote, "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength," captures one of Stoicism's central lessons: lasting strength begins within. External circumstances will always change, but a disciplined mind can remain steady through success and failure alike.Whether readers first encountered Marcus Aurelius through history books, philosophy or Gladiator, his words continue to offer practical guidance for navigating modern life. In an age filled with distractions, uncertainty and constant noise, his reminder to focus on what truly lies within our control is as valuable today as it was in ancient Rome.
Article Summary: Marcus Aurelius ruled the Roman Empire from AD 161 until his death in AD 180. He is remembered as the last of Rome's "Five Good Emperors" Despite carrying enormous responsibilities, he found time to write personal reflections that would later become Meditations, one of history's most influential philosophical works.

Article Title: Two killed after small plane crashes into house in Germany
Article Text:
Emergency services at the scene after a small plane crashed lodged in the roof of a house, in Ganderkesee

Two men were killed after a small private aircraft crashed into the roof of a house in northwestern Germany on Saturday, police said.The light aircraft went down in a residential neighbourhood in Ganderkesee, near the city of Oldenburg, before crashing head-on into the pitched roof of a home, reported AFP.Police had initially confirmed one fatality and said the second occupant was missing. However, after what authorities described as a lengthy and complex recovery operation to remove the wreckage embedded in the house, both occupants were confirmed dead.The victims, aged 65 and 77, were from the city of Bremen.Residents of the house had been evacuated as emergency crews worked to recover the aircraft. They were allowed to return after the wreckage was removed.German authorities have launched an investigation to determine what caused the crash.
Article Summary: The light aircraft went down in a residential neighbourhood in Ganderkesee, near the city of Oldenburg. It crashed head-on into the pitched roof of a home. Police had initially confirmed one fatality and said the second occupant was missing.

Article Title: South Korea chipmakers to supply US firms in $950 billion deals
Article Text:
The announcement was made as President Lee Jae Myung visited San Francisco for talks with heads of major US tech firms

South Korean memory chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK hynix will supply US tech companies, including Nvidia, in agreements worth $950 billion, a presidential adviser said on Saturday. The announcement was made as President Lee Jae Myung visited San Francisco for talks with the heads of major US technology companies, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and Broadcom's Hock Tan.The two Korean chip giants and US tech firms agreed to "pursue cooperation" in the sector, said presidential chief of staff for policy Kim Yong-beom. South Korea is home to the world's leading memory chipmakers, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, whose advanced memory chips are essential to the rapidly evolving AI industry and have fuelled optimism about the country's economic outlook.(This is an AFP story)
Article Summary: South Korean memory chip giants Samsung and SK hynix will supply US tech companies, including Nvidia, in agreements worth $950 billion. The announcement was made as President Lee Jae Myung visited San Francisco for talks with the heads of major US technology companies.

Article Title: Ukraine killed 11 in tourist camp: Russia
Article Text:
Russia claims Ukraine killed 11 people (Representative image)

Russian refinery and oil platform hit, says Ukraine

Russian authorities said 11 people, including four children, were killed by Ukraine in an overnight attack on a holiday camp in a Russian-held part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, accusing Kyiv on Saturday of deliberately attacking civilians.Ukraine did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Ukraine launched more than 300 drones, Moscow said, killing at least two people in a border region and hitting as far as the Urals city of Yekaterinburg.Ukraine said on Saturday its drones had hit a Russian oil platform in the Caspian Sea and an oil refinery in Siberia, while both Kyiv and Moscow said they had struck ships carrying military cargo.The energy targets lie over 700km and 2,000km from Ukrainian territory, underscoring the increasing reach of Kyiv's campaign to use long-range drones to undermine Russia's war effort and pressure the Kremlin to make peace.Ukraine struck the Filanovsky oil platform belonging to Russia's Lukoil. The platform is part of Russia's largest Caspian oil field.In the Black Sea, Russia's defence ministry said its drones had hit a bulk carrier delivering military cargo for the Ukrainian army. reuters
Article Summary: Russian authorities say 11 people, including four children, were killed by Ukraine in an overnight attack on a holiday camp in a Russian-held part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. Ukraine launched more than 300 drones, Moscow said, killing at least two people in a border region and hitting as far as the Urals city of Yekaterinburg.

Article Title: Iran-backed Houthis fire missiles at Saudi Arabia in response to airstrikes in Yemen
Article Text:
Saudi authorities issued emergency warnings for the provinces of Jazan and Yanbu

CAIRO: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said Saturday that they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi airstrikes on the strategic Red Sea city of Hodeida, in an escalation over vital shipping routes in the Middle East while the United States and Iran vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz.Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, the Houthis' military spokesperson, said in a prerecorded statement that the attack targeted facilities in the Red Sea cities of Yanbu and Jizan that belong to Aramco, the world's largest oil company.Saudi Arabia's civil defense said alerts sounded multiple times early Saturday in both cities, but the kingdom didn't comment further.There were no reported strikes overnight in Iran, in an apparent break from nearly two weeks of consecutive nights of U.S.attacks.Red Sea escalation further threatens global shipping The Houthis have said they would close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Saudi-linked shipping in retaliation for the kingdom's blockade on Yemen and a recent attack on the international airport in Yemen's rebel-held capital, Sanaa."Nothing short of ending the aggression and lifting the blockade, otherwise, it's all illusion and mirage," Mahdi al-Mashat, head of the Houthi-led Supreme Political Council governing rebel-controlled territories in Yemen, said of what it would take for the Houthis to not blockade the Bab-El-Mandeb.That strait, at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, is a vital shipping chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Around 12% of the world's trade, including a quarter of its container traffic, passes through the narrows.The Houthis targeted two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea this week. In response, Saudi Arabia struck Hodeida, the Saudi-led coalition opposing the rebels said Saturday. The strikes late Friday hit the port and the state-run telecommunications corporation, injuring two people, said Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run health ministry.The Saudi-led coalition said it didn't hit the port but struck "legitimate military targets" in Hodeida province that "were linked to threats to commercial vessels in the Red Sea."Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, called for "diplomacy and dialogue" to solve the Yemen conflict without "military confrontations" in an interview published Saturday by the state-run newspaper called Iran.Iran condemns Ukrainian attack on commercial vessel "Iran had a peaceful night," Hossein Kermanpour, a spokesperson for Iran's Health Ministry, posted on X. U.S. Central Command didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Unlike the previous 13 nights, it didn't announce new strikes.But Iran's foreign ministry condemned what it called a Ukrainian attack Saturday on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, saying one person was killed and another was hurt and calling it an act of aggression.In a separate statement, Araghchi said he spoke with European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas about it and that Tehran demanded a response. Ukraine's diplomatic representative to Iran was summoned, Iranian state media reported.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy earlier said on X that Ukraine "achieved very strong results with long‑range strikes in the Caspian Sea - including vessels used in military cargo shipments involving Iran."While efforts at mediation between the U.S. and Iran continue, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu plans to travel to the United States next week and meet with President Donald Trump in Washington on Tuesday, his office said Friday. They last met in Washington in February, weeks before they launched the war.Over 7,000 people have been killed, including in Lebanon A tenuous ceasefire that halted major operations for weeks has seemed to unravel this month. The U.S. accused Iran of striking three ships in the Strait of Hormuz and responded by striking dozens of targets in Iran, which retaliated by firing at U.S.-allied Gulf Arab states.The U.S. military has renewed its blockade of Iran's ports. Iran's Revolutionary Guard has advised residents of neighboring countries to stay away from bases with U.S. troops.The war has killed more than 3,400 people in Iran, according to its Health Ministry. Eighteen U.S. service members, 24 civilians in Israel and smaller numbers of civilians including foreign workers and mariners have been reportedly killed across the region.In Lebanon, more than 4,000 people have been killed since Iran-backed Hezbollah militants fired at Israel in support of the Islamic Republic two days after the war began and Israel responded with strikes and ground forces. Thirty-eight Israeli troops have also died.
Article Summary: Iran's foreign minister calls for "diplomacy and dialogue" to solve the Yemen conflict. Iran condemns a Ukrainian attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea. Saudi authorities issue emergency warnings for the provinces of Jazan and Yanbu. Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels say they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.

Article Title: Samurai quote of the day: 'You must understand that there is more than one path to the top of the mountain' and a timeless wisdom
Article Text:
Samurai quote of the day by Miyamoto Musashi

'You must understand that there is more than one path to the top of the mountain'

Meaning of the quote and the significance of the mountain

The samurai were the hereditary military nobility and warrior class of feudal Japan. Miyamoto Musashi was a Japanese swordsman, strategist, and philosopher born in the late sixteenth century. He is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished martial artists in history, having fought in over sixty duels without suffering a single defeat. His life spanned a transitional period in Japanese history, moving from the bloody civil wars of the Sengoku period into the long peace of the Tokugawa shogunate.Musashi began his career as a duelist at a very young age, killing his first opponent when he was just thirteen years old.As he traveled across Japan refining his skills, he eventually created his own unique style of fencing called Niten Ichi-ryu, which involved fighting with two swords simultaneously rather than holding a single blade with both hands. Later in life, Musashi withdrew from active combat to focus on painting, calligraphy, sculpture, and philosophy. Shortly before his death in a cave in 1645, he wrote down his life's philosophy in a text known as The Book of Five Rings.It is in this book that he wrote one of the greatest Samurai wisdom:There are many ways to do the same thing. And if all lead to success, the ways do not matter; the mountain matters. The quote about understanding that there is more than one path to the top of the mountain comes directly from Musashi's reflection on strategy, human growth, and spiritual discipline. At its core, the statement is a warning against dogmatic thinking and rigidity. Musashi believed that many people become overly attached to a single method, style, or set of rules, assuming that their chosen way is the only valid road to mastery.When applied to physical combat, the quote means that a true master must not rely on a single weapon or a single rigid fighting technique. A person who only knows how to use a single type of sword will fail when stripped of that sword. A strategist who insists on approaching every battle with the exact same tactic will inevitably be defeated by an opponent who can adapt. To Musashi, the ultimate goal of training was not to memorize specific moves, but to understand the universal nature of conflict and timing so deeply that one could succeed using any tool or approach available.Beyond martial arts, the metaphor of the mountain peak represents any ultimate goal, such as truth, self-mastery, personal success, or spiritual peace. The mountain peak remains fixed, but the routes up its sides are infinite. Some paths are steep and direct, requiring great physical strength. Other paths wind slowly around the slopes, relying on patience and endurance. Some routes require a person to navigate thick forests, while others demand climbing over open rock.Route vs destinationThe quote reminds us that the specific path a person takes is secondary to the actual climb. Two people can follow entirely different disciplines, rely on completely different life experiences, and hold different daily habits, yet both can achieve the exact same high level of wisdom and competence. Problems arise when people confuse the route for the destination. When someone becomes convinced that their specific path is the absolute only way to succeed, they often waste energy judging or opposing others who are simply climbing up a different side of the same mountain.Musashi observed this flaw frequently in the martial arts schools of his era. Many teachers claimed that their specific style was sacred and superior to all others. They taught fixed stances and ritualized movements that only worked in controlled environments. Musashi criticized this because it created a false sense of security. He argued that if a method does not work in a real, unpredictable situation, it is useless, no matter how prestigious its history might be.By encouraging people to look at the mountain rather than getting attached to one specific trail, Musashi promotes extreme adaptability. He advises individuals to remain flexible, open-minded, and pragmatic. If a chosen path becomes blocked by an unexpected landslide or cliff, an adaptable person does not sit down and give up, nor do they try to push through an impossible wall out of stubbornness. Instead, they simply step back, assess the terrain, and find a new way upward.Ultimately, the quote teaches self-reliance and broad perspective. It asks us to respect the diverse ways other people learn and grow, while encouraging us to find the specific approach that best fits our own nature and circumstances. Mastery is not about copying someone else's steps perfectly, but about reaching the summit through continuous effort, acute awareness, and unwavering resolve.
Article Summary: Miyamoto Musashi was a Japanese swordsman, strategist, and philosopher born in the late sixteenth century. He is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished martial artists in history, having fought in over sixty duels without suffering a single defeat. Musashi wrote down his life's philosophy in a text known as The Book of Five Rings.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Benjamin Franklin: 'Those who would give up essential liberty, to purchase a little temporary safety, deserve neither liberty nor safety' and a lesson on whether to choose freedom
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Benjamin Franklin.

'Those who would give up essential liberty, to purchase a little temporary safety, deserve neither liberty nor safety'

Freedom vs control

Who was Benjamin Franklin?

A statement that Benjamin Franklin said on a specific issue became a memorable quote over the years. The founding father of America wrote a letter on behalf of the Pennsylvania Assembly to the colony's governor in 1755. It was meant to be an economic and political statement about tax sovereignty. During the French and Indian War, the Pennsylvania Assembly wanted to tax the massive landholdings of the colony's proprietors (the Penn family) to fund defense on the frontier. The Penn family offered to pay a small lump sum for defense, provided the Assembly agreed to waive its right to tax their lands in the future.The Assembly refused the offer. In Franklin's mind, accepting a temporary handout ("a little temporary safety") in exchange for giving up the legislature's fundamental constitutional right to pass tax legislation ("essential liberty") was a dangerous trade.He wrote:But the quote became a memorable saying on the danger of trading fundamental rights for short-term comfort.The quote implies that if you surrender core freedoms just because you are scared, the "safety" you get in return is fragile and fake. A system powerful enough to take your liberty will eventually use that power against you, leaving you with neither freedom nor protection.Absolute safety is impossible without total, authoritarian control. To live in a truly free society, citizens must accept a certain amount of vulnerability. You cannot build a completely risk-free world without building a cage.People rarely surrender their rights when they are calm; they do it when they are panicked. The quote acts as a warning against letting immediate crises or fear drive permanent, structural changes to a society.Franklin's quote speaks about the choice between freedom and control. It reminds us that fear makes people vulnerable to bad deals. When people are frightened, they are often willing to hand over fundamental rights to anyone who promises to protect them. But absolute safety is impossible to achieve, and the control granted during a crisis usually remains long after the danger has passed. The quote serves as a lasting reminder that trading away fundamental human rights for short-term comfort usually leaves a society with less freedom and no real protection in the end.Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) was one of the most remarkable polymaths in history — a true polymath who excelled as a writer, inventor, scientist, diplomat, and statesman. He is celebrated as one of the key Founding Fathers of the United States. He was the only founding father to sign all four key founding documents: Declaration of Independence (1776), Treaty of Alliance with France (1778), Treaty of Paris ending the Revolutionary War (1783), US Constitution (1787).Franklin was internationally famous for his scientific experiments long before he entered revolutionary politics. His famous kite-and-key experiment proved that lightning is a form of electricity. He coined common electrical terms still used today, including battery, charge, positive, and negative. Despite his massive influence on the creation of the presidency and the government, Franklin was never President of the United States. However, his face has graced the $100 bill since 1914.
Article Summary: Franklin's quote speaks about the choice between freedom and control. It reminds us that fear makes people vulnerable to bad deals. To live in a truly free society, citizens must accept a certain amount of vulnerability. You cannot build a completely risk-free world without building a cage.

Article Title: A rural Chile community struggling with drought restored its water supply by protecting a watershed, planting native trees and rebuilding the soil that holds rain
Article Text:
​Rural community on Chile's Chiloé Island restores its water supply. (Picture: Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity)

A rainy island faced shortages

Restoring nature

Even during the lowest measured summer flows, the stream supplied around 6.3 gallons of water every minute. (Representational AI image)

A gravity-fed system

Wetland protected quality

Locally built and maintained

Poll Vote & Share your view Which element of the Catruman community water project do you find most admirable? Community cooperation Environmental restoration Innovative gravity-fed system 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A small rural community on Chile's Chiloe Island has ended years of dependence on emergency water tanker trucks by restoring its forests, protecting its watershed and building a community-managed water system.The project took years of planning and work by local residents, researchers and landowners. Rather than only building pipes and storage tanks, the community focused on improving the health of the land that supplies water. Nearly seven years after the system began operating, residents continue to receive a reliable water supply.The experience has now been turned into a practical guide for other rural communities that are facing water shortages.While the exact model cannot be copied everywhere, the approach of protecting the water source before building infrastructure can be adapted to many places. The information was published by Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity.Chiloe Island is known for heavy rainfall. The Ancud area receives around 87 inches of rain in an average year. Even so, the Catruman community experienced serious water shortages.The problem was not the total amount of rainfall but when it fell. Most rain comes during winter, while summer rainfall has reduced over the years. During the dry season, small streams can stop flowing for as long as four months.As a result, many families struggled to get enough water. Before the project started, 64% of households depended partly on water supplied by tanker trucks. Around 37% relied completely on tanker deliveries for six months or more.Municipal records from the 2014-2015 drought show that tanker deliveries provided an average of only 2.4 gallons of water per person each day. That limited amount had to cover drinking, cooking, washing, caring for animals and watering vegetable gardens.To solve the problem, the community decided to improve the entire watershed. A watershed is the area of land where rainwater collects and flows into streams, rivers or springs. Keeping the land healthy helps water soak into the ground and flow steadily throughout the year.Residents worked with researchers to map Catruman's 36 microcatchments, small areas that collect rainwater. They identified a stream that flowed throughout the year and partnered with upstream landowners to protect it.The team planted more than 500 native trees around damaged land and an old spring. These included ulmo, coihue, canelo, luma and arrayan trees, all native to southern Chile.They also dug small infiltration trenches on slopes. These shallow channels slow down rainwater allowing more of it to soak into the soil instead of flowing away. This helps recharge groundwater and keeps streams flowing longer during dry periods.After protecting the water source, the community built a gravity-fed water supply system. Water is collected at an intake point, passes through filters and is stored in a tank with a capacity of about 6,600 gallons. From there, it flows downhill through pipes to homes using gravity, eliminating the need for electric pumps.Because the system uses gravity, it reduces electricity costs and ongoing maintenance, making it more suitable for a small rural community.Even during the lowest measured summer flows, the stream supplied around 6.3 gallons of water every minute, or about 9,100 gallons each day.The estimated daily demand for 14 families and the local civic centre was about 2,640 gallons. This meant enough water remained in the stream to support the surrounding ecosystem.The project also focused on keeping the water clean. A constructed wetland was built near a home and a small cheese-making operation located upstream from the community's water intake.Constructed wetlands use plants and naturally occurring microorganisms to clean household wastewater. After treatment, the water can either be reused for irrigation or allowed to soak safely into the ground instead of flowing back into the community's water source.The project showed that increasing the amount of available water is only part of the challenge. Protecting water quality is equally important because pollution from wastewater, livestock or household activities can make a water source unsafe.Community members carried out much of the construction through traditional collective work gatherings known as 'mingas'.Residents also received training to maintain the pipes, filters and restoration areas. They formed a local organisation to collect fees, organise repairs and work with government agencies and landowners when needed.Community leader Galicia Mansilla said the changes had made a significant difference. "Before, we lived with a lot of uncertainty. Today, we have a system that works," Ecoticias reported.
Article Summary: Rural community on Chile's Chiloé Island restores its water supply. Project took years of planning and work by local residents, researchers and landowners. Rather than only building pipes and storage tanks, the community focused on improving the health of the land that supplies water. The experience has now been turned into a practical guide for other rural communities that are facing water shortages.

Article Title: 'Credible threat' from Iran proxies forced Trump to switch planes mid-trip: Report
Article Text: US President Donald Trump switched from a new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 to the older Air Force One before departing Turkey earlier this month, according to reports. The move came after US officials identified what they described as a "credible threat" from Iranian proxy forces targeting the president.The New York Times reported earlier that the threat emerged while Trump was attending the Nato summit in Ankara. He had arrived aboard the newly inducted Boeing 747-8, gifted by Qatar, which does not have the same advanced defensive systems as the legacy Air Force One aircraft.Citing people familiar with the matter, the report claimed that after US officials detected the threat, the US secret service recommended that Trump change aircraft before leaving Turkey.The report said the intelligence indicated that Iranian proxy forces were targeting Trump himself rather than the aircraft. However, the newer Boeing's comparatively limited defensive capabilities made flying on it a greater security risk.CBS News confirmed the report later on Friday, saying the US secret service decided to switch planes after receiving intelligence about "a credible plot to fire a missile at the plane".Trump flew to Ankara aboard the new Boeing 747-8, a $400 million Boeing 747-8 that the US accepted as a gift from the Qatari government last year and spent months retrofitting to prepare for it to carry the president. However, after the summit concluded, the US president flew from Ankara to the United Kingdom in the old Air Force One, before switching back to the newer plane to complete his trip back to the United States.The decision prompted fresh questions about the security capabilities of the new aircraft. Citing sources familiar with the matter, the broadcaster reported that the older Air Force One is equipped with laser technology to blind incoming missiles, along with systems designed to misdirect incoming munitions and other defensive countermeasures. It added that it remains unclear what defensive systems are installed on the newer Qatari-donated jet.Earlier this month, Trump did not disclose the security reason behind the aircraft switch, saying he would use the older Air Force One "for old time's sake". He also told reporters that the new aircraft already "has a lot of capability" but would be "maxed out" over the next month as additional upgrades were completed.Trump has repeatedly referred to alleged Iranian threats against his life in recent months. He has previously said he left standing orders for the US military to destroy Iran "at levels they've never seen before" if Tehran carried out what he described as longstanding threats to assassinate him.The latest revelations also come as Trump weighs further military action against Iran following the collapse of a recent ceasefire. Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday, Trump said, "We are talking to them. I ​think they're being ​serious. I think ... they are ‌being ⁠by far the most serious that we've seen them, but ​that doesn't ​mean ⁠we get there. We'll see ​what happens." He added, "We're locked and loaded. We're ready to go."
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump switched from a new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 to the older Air Force One. The move came after US officials identified what they described as a "credible threat" from Iranian proxy forces targeting the president. The decision prompted fresh questions about the security capabilities of the new aircraft.

Article Title: In 1904, Newfoundland released four moose to attract hunters; their population later reached 200,000 and began reshaping the island’s forests
Article Text:
Moose occur naturally in Labrador but not on the island of Newfoundland.

Why moose population grew quickly

Moose changed forests

Category I –1.0 moose per km2, Category I – 1.5 moose per km2, and Category I – 2.0 moose per km2

The first major decline

History repeats in 1990s

Finding balance

More than a century ago, Newfoundland, an island in Canada, introduced just a handful of moose to its forests to create hunting opportunities and provide a reliable source of meat. The animals multiplied into one of the largest moose populations in North America and permanently reshape the island's forests.The story began in 1878, when moose were first brought to the island, and continued in 1904 with the release of four more animals. Over the following decades, the population grew rapidly. With abundant food, almost no natural predators and vast forests to roam, the animals spread across the island much faster than expected.Today, wildlife managers say the moose are an important part of Newfoundland's culture and economy, but they also serve as a reminder of what can happen when a species grows beyond what its habitat can support. The province's 2022-2026 Moose Management Plan explains how the population expanded, why it later declined and how science is now helping keep the animals and their habitat in balance.Moose occur naturally in Labrador but not on the island of Newfoundland.According to the management plan, the introduced animals found ideal conditions after arriving on the island.There were no other large plant-eating animals competing for the same food. At the same time, wolves, the moose's main natural predator, had almost disappeared and the Newfoundland wolf became extinct around 1930. Young forests created by natural disturbances also provided plenty of fresh vegetation for the animals to eat.These favourable conditions allowed the population to increase rapidly. By the late 1950s, the island's moose population is estimated to have reached between 150,000 and 200,000, giving Newfoundland one of the highest moose densities in the world.Moose are large animals that eat huge amounts of vegetation every day. An adult moose consumes around 20 to 30 kilograms of plants daily. Across Newfoundland, that adds up to about one million tonnes of plant material every year. The animals mainly feed on young trees, shrubs and other new growth that are also essential for forests to regenerate.Wildlife managers say forests can provide only a limited amount of food. When moose numbers grow too high, they eat plants faster than the vegetation can recover, leaving less food available over time.Scientists call this the habitat's carrying capacity, meaning the maximum number of animals the land can support without being damaged. Once that limit is crossed, both the forests and the moose population begin to suffer.By the late 1950s and early 1960s, the island was already showing signs of over-browsing, where moose had eaten too much vegetation in many areas. Localised overhunting in some regions added to the problem.Although records from that period are limited, the management plan says the population may have fallen to less than 50,000 by the early 1970s.The decline prompted the provincial government to introduce an area-based quota system in 1973, allowing wildlife managers to control hunting in different regions according to local conditions. That system is still used today.The new approach helped reduce hunting pressure where moose numbers were already low while allowing greater harvests in areas where populations remained high. As habitats slowly recovered, the moose population also began to increase again.Over the next 25 years, moose numbers rose once more. Commercial forestry also created young forests that provided fresh food for the animals.By the 1990s, the population had again crossed 150,000. However, scientists say the island's forests could not continue supporting such large numbers.Unlike the sharp crash seen in the 1960s, wildlife managers had already started increasing hunting quotas in many areas to reduce pressure on habitats. As a result, the second decline was less severe.From the mid-1990s to 2012, Newfoundland's moose population declined by about 25 per cent. The management plan says the drop was seen even in areas where hunting was banned, suggesting that habitat limits, rather than hunting alone, were the main reason for the decline.The management plan estimates that Newfoundland's moose population is now about 110,000. Officials say the goal is not to return to the record numbers of the past but to maintain a healthy balance between moose, forests and people.Managers monitor populations using aerial surveys, hunter reports, jawbone collection programmes and other scientific information. These tools help estimate population size, breeding success, habitat conditions and harvest levels before hunting quotas are set for each management area.Different parts of the province also have different population targets. Areas close to major highways and population centres are managed for lower moose densities to help reduce the risk of vehicle collisions, while other regions are managed according to local habitat conditions.
Article Summary: Moose were introduced to Newfoundland in 1878 to provide a source of meat. Over the following decades, the population grew rapidly. By the late 1950s, the island's moose population is estimated to have reached between 150,000 and 200,000, giving Newfoundland one of the highest moose densities in the world. The population has since declined by about 25 per cent.

Article Title: Donald Trump returns to White House Correspondents' dinner months after shooting forced postponement
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump attends the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner

US President Donald Trump on Friday attended the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) dinner, nearly three months after the annual event was postponed following a shooting outside the original venue.The US president is set to address journalists from major news organisations after months of clashes with the media over coverage and press access.Ahead of the event, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said Trump's remarks would be "a combination of unifying yet vicious, and serious yet hilarious, all at the same time."The annual black-tie dinner, which celebrates press freedom and raises money for journalism scholarships, was postponed from April after a gunman attempted to breach a security checkpoint and opened fire outside the venue room at Washington Hilton, where Trump and members of his Cabinet were present.Friday's event is now being held at the Waldorf Astoria hotel under heightened security.Meanwhile, the suspect in the shooting, Cole Allen, later pleaded not guilty to charges including attempting to assassinate the president.The White House Correspondents' Association said the programme would include recognition of Secret Service officer Victor Gonzales, who was wounded while stopping the attacker, as well as Washington Hilton staff who assisted guests during the incident.Trump's appearance comes amid continued criticism from press freedom advocates over his administration's lawsuits against media organisations, restrictions on some journalists' access and other actions affecting the press. The White House has defended those measures, saying they are intended to improve accountability, protect sensitive information and address media bias.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump attended the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) dinner. The annual black-tie dinner was postponed from April after a gunman attempted to breach a security checkpoint and opened fire outside the venue room at Washington Hilton. The event is now being held at the Waldorf Astoria hotel under heightened security.

Article Title: Pentagon under fire after revising Iran war casualty count
Article Text:
Photo credit: NYC

The Pentagon has come under scrutiny after reducing the official death toll of US service members killed in the Iran war from 18 to 14 on its website, triggering criticism from military families, veterans and lawmakers over the transparency of its casualty reporting.According to a The New York Times report, the four service members recently killed in Jordan and Iraq were removed from the official tally because they died after President Donald Trump declared a ceasefire, despite the president publicly citing the total number of war dead as 18 days earlier.The acting press secretary for the Pentagon, Joel Valdez, on Thursday attributed the change to “temporary data disruptions” on the website that he suggested would be quickly fixed.The revised casualty count has sparked criticism from military families, veterans and democratic lawmakers, who accused the Pentagon of failing to provide a transparent and timely accounting of the human cost of the conflict.“It is truly disgusting and disheartening to lower the count of our service members who gave their life for this country,” said Tanya Stamos, a Navy veteran and the founder of Operation RJS.She further stated, “As a Navy combat veteran myself, I find it a slap in the face that it is so easy to disregard my brothers and sisters in arms who raised their hand and gave an oath to protect and serve foreign and domestic, all for the government who is choosing to wipe their names from history.”A group of democratic senators has written to defense secretary Pete Hegseth seeking a comprehensive accounting of US personnel killed or wounded during the Iran war, arguing that the American public, Congress and military families are entitled to accurate casualty reporting.After nearly five months of fighting, 18 US service members have been killed in the Iran war. The majority of the fatalities occurred during the conflict's early phase, when Iranian missile and drone attacks targeted American bases across Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Jordan.Nine service members were killed in those attacks, while another six died on March 12 when a US air force KC-135 aerial refuelling aircraft crashed in western Iraq during operational missions.A US navy sailor later died after a helicopter made an emergency landing in the Arabian Sea on July 1, taking the official death toll to 14 before the latest escalation.The remaining four deaths occurred after fighting resumed following the collapse of the ceasefire. On July 18, Iranian ballistic missiles struck Muwaffaq Salti air base in Jordan, killing 3 US service members. A day later, another US service member was killed at Erbil air base in Iraq during the controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian drone.
Article Summary: Pentagon has reduced the official death toll of US service members killed in the Iran war from 18 to 14. Four service members recently killed in Jordan and Iraq were removed from the official tally because they died after President Donald Trump declared a ceasefire. The acting press secretary for the Pentagon, Joel Valdez, on Thursday attributed the change to “temporary data disruptions” on the website.

Article Title: Trump wears '2028' cap at White House dinner, says 'third time will be better'
Article Text:
Trump dons 'Trump 2028' cap

US president Donald Trump on Friday (local time) joked about seeking a third term while addressing the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) Dinner, before quickly clarifying that he was "only kidding. "During his remarks, Trump likened the delayed event to his second term, saying both were better the second time around."I am delighted to be here at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. Just like my presidency, the second time is always better. It's always better. And the third time will be better yet," the US president said.Trump later added that he was "only kidding" about the idea.Toward the end of his speech, Trump put on a red cap reading "Trump 2028" and jokingly announced the "scoop" that he was running for president again.Later in his remarks, Trump quipped that next year's White House Correspondents' Dinner could be named after him, claiming that Paramount Skydance chief executive David Ellison had floated the idea."Next year, they're going to call it the Trump White House Correspondents' Dinner," Trump said. "(Ellison) told me that, and I like that very much. We're going to change the name of it, okay?"The US Constitution's 22nd Amendment bars any individual from being elected president more than twice.Trump is currently serving his second term in the White House.Despite the constitutional limit on presidential terms, Trump has repeatedly hinted in recent months at the possibility of remaining in office beyond his second term.Ratified in 1951, the 22nd Amendment explicitly states that "no person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice.The White House Correspondents' Dinner was rescheduled after its original April date was cancelled following a major security breach at the Washington Hilton.According to authorities, a man identified as Cole Allen allegedly ran through a security checkpoint carrying loaded firearms and knives before being confronted by US Secret Service agents outside the ballroom. Officials said Allen allegedly assaulted an officer before being restrained, while Trump and senior administration officials were rushed to safety after gunfire was reported outside the venue.Allen has pleaded not guilty to four federal charges, including attempting to assassinate a president and assaulting a law enforcement officer.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump joked about seeking a third term while addressing the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) Dinner. Trump later added that he was "only kidding" about the idea. The US Constitution's 22nd Amendment bars any individual from being elected president more than twice.

Article Title: What is an EB-1 visa? Why is it narrowing for Indians in FY 2026?
Article Text:
State Department says EB-1 may become unavailable for Indians for FY 2026.

What is the current waiting period for Indians for EB-1 vsa?

Cutoff Date:

Filing/Application Date:

Wait Time:

Why is the EB-1 category getting so many applications from India?

An EB-1 visa (Employment-Based First Preference) is a top-tier US permanent residency (Green Card) category. It is intended for individuals with extraordinary ability, outstanding professors or researchers, and multinational managers or executives. EB-1 used to be the fastest Green Card route as it had little or zero backlog as it is not taken by the maximum -- because they don't qualify for it.But in the August visa bulletin, the State Department warned that EB-1 may become unavailable for Indians in FY 206 which ends in September. "High demand and number use by aliens chargeable to India in the EB-1 visa category may necessitate making the category unavailable in the coming weeks if India’s pro-rated limit in the EB-1 category is reached before the fiscal year ends.This situation will be continually monitored, and any necessary adjustments will be made accordingly," the department said.People from India receiving their EB-1 Green Cards now submitted their initial petitions (their Priority Date) on or before October 15, 2022.The official cutoff date (Final Action Date) for Indian applicants in the EB-1 category is October 15, 2022.The individuals getting their Green Cards approved today initially submitted their Form I-140 (Immigrant Petition) or established their priority date around late 2022 or earlier.This corresponds to an effective processing wait time of approximately 3.5 to 4 years for Indian nationals in the EB-1 category.Many EB-2 and EB-3 applicants are switching to EB-1 who are eligible to get Green Cards faster, which is intensifying the competition. There is little spillover from the family-based quotas to the EB-1 category as well.There are three types of EB-1 visas: First is for top scientists, founders, artists and athletes, Second is for university professors, senior researchers and third is for corporate VPs, directors and senior managers.
Article Summary: EB-1 used to be the fastest Green Card route as it had little or zero backlog as it is not taken by the maximum -- because they don't qualify for it. But in the August visa bulletin, the State Department warned that EB- 1 may become unavailable for Indians in FY 206 which ends in September. "High demand and number use by aliens chargeable to India may necessitate making the category unavailable in the coming weeks," the department said.

Article Title: ‘Nothing compares to home, but…’: Indian man explains why many people end up staying in US
Article Text:
Gaurav Makhloga explains why many people end up staying in the US instead of returning.

An Indian man living in the United States has spoken about why many people who move abroad with short-term plans to return home often end up settling there permanently, citing work prospects, lifestyle changes and the overall living environment as key factors.Gaurav Makhloga shared his thoughts in a video posted on Instagram, reflecting on how his outlook changed after relocating to the US.He said that before leaving India, he believed he would spend a few years earning money in America before returning home to settle down.However, he said his experience after moving was different from what he had expected.In the video, Makhloga highlighted the peaceful surroundings in his neighbourhood, showing quiet streets and green open spaces during the evening.He said the calm environment made him understand why many people struggle to leave after building a life in the country."Before coming to America, my plan was simply to spend a few years here, then head back home and enjoy life. But look at what I found here," he said.He added that while nothing could replace one's homeland, the quality of life in the US often influences people's decisions to remain there.Makhloga also said professional opportunities and modern infrastructure were major factors behind that choice, arguing that they offer a level of convenience many immigrants value after settling abroad.Despite praising life in the US, he acknowledged the emotional connection people have with their native country, saying there is no substitute for one's own home.
Article Summary: Gaurav Makhloga shared his thoughts in a video posted on Instagram. He said that before leaving India, he believed he would spend a few years in the US. However, he said his experience after moving was different from what he had expected.

Article Title: Atelise launching soon, utilizing India’s craftsmanship for the future of personalized fashion
Article Text:
.

Atelise, a new custom clothing platform, is launching soon with a mission to make high-quality, bespoke fashion more globally and financially accessible while celebrating the craftsmanship of India’s tailors, artisans, and designers.Founded by Priyanka Venkannagari, a Stanford MBA and former COO with experience building operations across global markets, and Tara Paranjpe, a product leader with a decade of experience building platforms and marketplaces at global scale, Atelise is creating the future of personalization in fashion. The platform allows customers to design custom clothing by choosing silhouettes, fabrics, finishing details, and fit preferences, while connecting them with skilled tailors who can bring each garment to life.At a time when fast fashion dominates global wardrobes, Atelise is taking a different approach: clothing made only after a customer orders it, designed around individual fit and personal style. The company aims to reduce waste, support artisan livelihoods, and give customers access to clothing that feels both personal and beautifully made.India is central to Atelise’s launch. With its deep textile heritage, skilled tailoring networks, and centuries-old craft traditions, India offers a unique foundation for the future of personalized fashion.From hand embroidery and block printing to Banarasi borders, silk weaving, intricate beadwork, and modern tailoring, the country’s craftsmanship has long shaped global fashion. Atelise hopes to bring these skills to a new generation of customers outside of India, who want access to clothing that is beautiful, personal, meaningful, and made with care.The platform is currently looking to collaborate with Indian tailors, designers, boutiques, embroiderers, fabric suppliers, and small production studios. Atelise is especially interested in partners who can work on bespoke garments, custom westernwear dresses, occasion wear, menswear, resort wear, and everyday pieces with a high level of finishing and attention to detail.For designers, Atelise offers an opportunity to share original designs with a broader audience and receive commissions when customers order their pieces. For tailors and production partners, the platform aims to create a new channel for consistent custom work, connecting them with customers who value craftsmanship and fit.For customers in markets where bespoke has largely disappeared, Atelise offers a more personal alternative to traditional online shopping. Instead of searching endlessly for the right size or settling for standard designs, customers can begin with an idea, inspiration image, fabric, or design template and work toward a garment made specifically for them. The company has already produced more than 100 custom pieces, with the founders working directly with customers to test the experience before opening the platform more widely.“Atelise is built on the belief that clothing should be made for you, not simply sold to you,” the company said. “India has some of the most talented craftspeople in the world, and we want to build a platform that helps connect that talent with customers globally.”Custom clothing has long been seen as expensive, slow, and hard to access. Atelise pairs technology and design support with a trusted network of makers so ordering a custom piece feels as simple as it should.The company is building tools that help customers visualize designs before ordering, capture measurements more accurately, and communicate clearly with makers. By combining digital design with human craftsmanship, Atelise wants to create a smoother bridge between inspiration and a finished garment.As Atelise grows, the company plans to expand its network across India and other artisan-rich markets, while continuing to onboard customers who are looking for custom clothing for weddings, holidays, events, workwear, and everyday wardrobes.Atelise is currently inviting Indian tailors, designers, and artisan partners to join its maker network. The company is also welcoming early customers who want to create custom clothing and be part of the platform’s launch community.With its focus on fit, craft, and bespoke production, Atelise hopes to reimagine what global fashion can look like when technology supports, rather than replaces, the hands behind the garment.
Article Summary: Atelise, a new custom clothing platform, is launching soon with a mission to make high-quality, bespoke fashion more globally and financially accessible. The platform allows customers to design custom clothing by choosing silhouettes, fabrics, finishing details, and fit preferences, while connecting them with skilled tailors who can bring each garment to life.

Article Title: Only in America: Amid the roast, Trump toasts free speech
Article Text:
Donald Trump at White House correspondent's dinner (Image/AP)

TOI correspondent from Washington:

It was as though a bull had been invited to hand out prizes at a china convention. The White House Correspondents' Association's rescheduled annual dinner on Friday night produced one of those deliciously improbable scenes that remind the world why American democracy is equal parts constitutional republic and absurdist theatre.There sat President Donald Trump, who has spent years suing, skewering, ridiculing and generally treating journalists the way a cobra views a mongoose, applauding Wall Street Journal reporters as they collected an award for investigating... Donald Trump.The Journal team received the WHCA's Katharine Graham Award for Courage and Accountability for reporting on Trump's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. CNN's Wolf Blitzer, introducing the award, reminded the audience – in front of the President – that the reporting had triggered lawsuits, retaliation and personal consequences for reporters.“Trump quickly filed a $20 billion lawsuit against the Journal, revealing reporter Khadeeja Safdar’s home address. Her family had to be relocated. The Journal was kicked off of Air Force One,” Blitzer told the gathering, as the President threw up his hands and essayed a wry smile.Only in America could the First Amendment receive an acknowledgement from one of its most trenchant litigants. Try staging that in half the world's capitals and the dinner menu would consist mainly of prison food.Then came the piece de resistance: Trump smiling, rising, shaking hands with the very journalists whose work he insists is false and whose newspaper he is still battling in court. He had promised he had toned down the speech prepared for April, but Washington quickly discovered that the MAGA boss' definition of restraint resembles a chainsaw fitted with a muffler.He torched through an hour of familiar terrain, firing jibes and jeers at journalists, tv personalities, and assorted political enemies with the confidence of a man who has never met a microphone he didn't like. He ribbed reporters about their coverage and joked about a third presidential term (his favorite fantasy).To critics, however, the evening looked less like democratic resilience and more like Washington's oldest bad habit —debating the menu when the kitchen is on fire. They argued that sharing jokes, champagne, and applause with a President who continues to sue news organizations and threaten broadcasters risks making the extraordinary appear routine.The evening itself was a sequel nobody wanted but everyone felt obliged to attend. The original April gala at the Washington Hilton ended in chaos when an armed man tried to breach security, forcing Secret Service officers into action.Friday's do-over moved to the Waldorf Astoria under security so tight that even satire needed credentials. Roughly 700 guests, a third of the usual crowd, threaded their way through multiple checkpoints before settling beneath glittering chandeliers that have witnessed many awkward dinners but none quite so exquisitely ironic.A few Trump jokes landed like guided missiles; most disappeared into the ballroom carpet with all the force of damp confetti. The audience, mostly grim-faced, laughed occasionally, the way one laughs at Thanksgiving when an argumentative uncle starts discussing politics after his third glass of wine.Yet after the jokes fade, one image will probably endure. Not the red "Trump 2028" hat, not the insults, not even the political punchlines. It will be the sight of a President, not famous for his grace or eloquence, applauding reporters who investigated him.
Article Summary: The Wall Street Journal received the Katharine Graham Award for Courage and Accountability for reporting on Trump's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. CNN's Wolf Blitzer reminded the audience – in front of the President – that the reporting had triggered lawsuits, retaliation and personal consequences for reporters.

Article Title: New details emerge about NYC stabber Raul Morales: Quran, Bible, book on Che Guevara, Marx found from his apartment
Article Text:
New details emerge about NYC staber Raul Morales.

One stabbing after another

The 51-year-old man, Raul Morales, who stabbed a Jewish man and an Asian man on Manhattan's Upper West Side, was charged with hate crime. New details emerged Saturday as his Amsterdam Avenue shared apartment was searched and writings of Marx were found. New York Post reported that two Qurans, a Jehovah's Witness Bible and a book on Cuban revolutionary Che Guevara were also found.Morales was arraigned late Friday on two counts of second-degree attempted murder as a hate crime; and one count each of first-degree assault as a hate crime, second-degree assault as a hate crime, and attempted first-degree assault as a hate crime, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office said.On Thursday, Morales first approached a 57-year-old Asian man from behind and shouted “Allahu Akbar” and stabbed him in the back with a knife, a prosecutor said at his late Friday arraignment, according to the district attorney’s office.Morales then continued walking and encountered a Jewish man wearing a kippah, a Jewish head covering, who had just left a synagogue, and stabbed him in the chest with a screwdriver, the prosecutor said in court, according to the prosecutor’s office.The first attack occurred around 84th Street and Central Park West, police said. The second happened at around 86th Street and Central Park West.Both victims are expected to survive.Language in the criminal complaint says that a witness saw Morales near a synagogue West 83rd Street saying “justice for Islam,” according to material from the district attorney’s office. There is no evidence that either victim knew each other or Morales.Morales' roommate said he told him that he was just going for a walk in the park. Morales did not appear angry or agitated. The neighbors also vouched that Morales did not come across as a violent person in their casual interactions.Morales apparently worked as a security guard in Brooklyn at least around 2007; he did two years in state prison on drug charges in the early 1990s and remained on probation for much of the decade,
Article Summary: Raul Morales, 51, was charged with two counts of second-degree attempted murder as a hate crime. Two Qurans, a Jehovah's Witness Bible and a book on Cuban revolutionary Che Guevara were also found in Morales' apartment.

Article Title: 'Way better than America's Independence Day': Texas influencer enraged by advertisement for Indian Independence Day event in Frisco
